title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated connectors can create, update and delete in third-party systems
summary: The briefing passes: its licensing, connector controls and approval model are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should clarify reusable approval duration, acknowledge conflicting guidance about Word and PowerPoint availability, and remove tool-inventory checklist steps that have no controls-table row.

claims.claim: The update unblocks federated connector create, update and delete tools in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: With this update, the connector tools that create, update, and delete content in those services are unblocked in Copilot Chat, so users can complete work without leaving Copilot.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.claim: Federated connectors query external services in real time.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Federated connectors were read-only before the October 2026 write-action change.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: A supported connector can turn an escalation email into a ticket or issue without leaving Copilot.
claims.quote: Users can complete work without leaving Copilot. For example, a user can turn an escalation email into an issue in a project-tracking tool

claims.claim: A supported connector can update a CRM record from Copilot.
claims.quote: update a record in a customer relationship management (CRM) system

claims.claim: A supported connector can add a comment to a ticket or issue from Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: or add a comment to a ticket directly from Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Actions use the user's source-system identity and cannot exceed that user's permissions.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.claim: The roadmap says every create, update or delete action requires explicit user confirmation.
claims.quote: every create, update, or delete action requires the user's explicit confirmation before it runs.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to Needs approval, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.

claims.claim: The confirmation card lets users review the action parameters before approval.
claims.quote: Users can expand the card to review the action parameters before approving it.

claims.claim: Nothing is sent to the connected system while an action is awaiting confirmation.
claims.quote: While an action is awaiting confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.

claims.claim: Allow once runs the action but requires approval the next time the tool is used.
claims.quote: Allow once | Runs the action now. Copilot asks again the next time it wants to use the tool.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses further approval prompts for that tool in the current conversation.
claims.quote: Allow for conversation | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.claim: Always allow permits later calls to the same tool without another prompt, subject to resetting approval.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cancel declines the action without changing the connected system.
claims.quote: Cancel | Declines the action. Nothing is changed in the connected system.

claims.claim: Reusable approvals apply to an individual tool, not the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.claim: New or changed write-capable tools are set to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: The roadmap says admins can inspect read and write/delete tools and disable connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.

claims.claim: Learn labels the admin-center connector tool view Coming soon.
claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon)

claims.claim: The admin-center tool list is not available for all connectors.
claims.quote: Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.claim: On a supported connector's details page, admins go to Tools, sign in to the service, and select All tools.
claims.quote:
On the connector's details page, go to the Tools section and sign in to the third-party service.

Select All tools, and then review the list to identify tools that can create, update, or delete data.

claims.claim: The admin tool list reflects the account used to sign in.
claims.quote: The tool list reflects the permissions of the account used to sign in.

claims.claim: Learn directs users to Copilot Settings > Sources > connector > Write/Delete tools when the admin tool view is unavailable.
claims.quote: sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot with your user account, go to Settings -> Sources, and select the connector. Then expand Write/Delete tools.

claims.claim: Admin-published connectors can create, update and delete using provided tools, with user approval and source permissions.

claims.quote: The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.quote: These actions export Customer Data to the connected system to create, update, delete, or otherwise modify data.

claims.claim: MCP servers restricting incoming traffic by source IP must allow Microsoft's static egress addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.quote: When appropriate, Microsoft 365 Copilot dynamically selects relevant tools to retrieve information or perform an action.

claims.claim: Always allow removes repeated confirmation for a user's tool indefinitely.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: '"Always allow" removes repeated confirmation for that tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.' The earlier paragraph already documents publisher-triggered resets; repeat that qualification here instead of 'indefinitely'.

claims.claim: Individual connector enable, disable and staged-rollout controls are under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for enabling, disabling or staging a federated connector is documented.

claims.claim: Publisher-type access applies to future connectors of that type while allowing individual staged-rollout exceptions.
claims.quote: Connectors of that type released later aren't available to users. To make a specific connector available, open it in Your connections and set its staged rollout to the users or groups you want.
